column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
If you could drain the ocean, what kinds of landscape would you see, and what would be the deepest and longest features?
Which part of the ocean floor is shallow and rich in fish and oil, and which is the steep drop beyond it?
What makes the sea surface rise and fall, and what do the high and low parts of a wave get called?
Which coastal landforms come from waves wearing the land away and which from waves laying material down?
What causes the giant destructive waves that sometimes follow an earthquake under the sea, and how high can they climb ashore?
On which phases of the Moon is the sea's rise and fall greatest, and why is it smallest at half-moon?
Why do ship captains check the tide table before docking, why do fishing communities care about high tide, and where might India generate power from tides?
What drives the great rivers of water in the ocean, and what decides whether we call one warm or cold?
Why does one northern harbour stay open to ships all winter while a port on a lower-latitude coast elsewhere can be blocked, and where are the richest fishing waters?
What is the job of a coastal alarm system for sudden sea hazards, and what should people be able to do once it sounds?
Describe the sequence from an undersea earthquake to a warning on a coastal resident's phone.
What has India built to protect people living on its coasts and those out at sea from cyclones?
Name resources the sea provides that are alive and others that are not, and what makes something a marine resource.
Why do millions of coastal people depend on the sea, and what must we be careful about while using it?
What three goals does a sustainable ocean-based economy try to balance?
Which global goal is about life in the oceans and what actions does it call for?
What can a country do in the sea nearest its coast, under what condition can foreign ships cross it, and what rights does it hold a bit further out?
Out to what distance does a coastal country have special rights to fish and oil, and who governs the sea beyond all countries' zones?
What are the 'traffic rules' for ships, and which agreement tries to stop ships polluting the sea?
What might happen at sea if there were no common rules for ships and countries?
